questions.expl: Aim at + V-ing (ou aim to + base verbale).

questions.q: The project aims ____ awareness.
questions.expl: Aim to + base verbale.

questions.q: I look forward ____ you at the exhibition.
questions.expl: Look forward to + V-ing.

questions.q: A student writes: "I look forward to see the exhibition." What is the mistake ?
choix: « to » is a preposition, so the verb must be seeing
« look » must be changed to looking here
« forward » needs the preposition at after it
« see » must take an -s in this sentence
questions.expl: Look forward to + V-ing : jamais de base verbale après ce « to ».

questions.q: Which sentence is correct ?
choix: She intends to move to Mexico.
She intends to moves to Mexico.
She intends at move to Mexico.
She intends for move to Mexico.
questions.expl: Intend to + base verbale, sans -s.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct ?
choix: The project aims to raise awareness.
The project aim to raise awareness.
The project aims to raising awareness.
The project aims at raise awareness.
questions.expl: Aim to + BV (avec le -s de la 3e personne) ; aim at + V-ing.

questions.q: Which sentence is INCORRECT ?
choix: They are looking forward to meet the artist.
They plan to meet the artist.
They intend to meet the artist.
They are planning on meeting the artist.
questions.expl: Seule la première est fausse : look forward to + V-ing (to meeting).

questions.q: Which constructions are followed by the base verbale (BV) ? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.expl: BV après intend to, plan to, aim to. V-ing après plan on, aim at et look forward to.

questions.q: Which constructions are followed by V-ing ? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.expl: V-ing après plan on, aim at et look forward to.

questions.q: Which verb expresses impatience, a positive expectation of a future event ?
questions.expl: Look forward to exprime l'impatience, l'attente positive.

questions.q: Which verb is the more formal one for a firm decision made in one's mind ?
questions.expl: Intend to : intention assez ferme, plus formelle que plan to.

questions.q: Which verb expresses a thought-out, organised project with concrete preparation ?
questions.expl: Plan to / plan on : un projet réfléchi, organisé.

questions.q: Which verb expresses a goal, an ambition to achieve ?
questions.expl: Aim to / aim at : un objectif, une ambition.

questions.q: In "I look forward to the exhibition", « to » can be followed by a noun.
questions.expl: Look forward to + V-ing ou un nom.

questions.q: Choose the correct translation: « Ce roman vise à dénoncer les termes péjoratifs utilisés pour désigner les immigrés. »
choix: This novel aims to denounce the derogatory terms used to speak about immigrants.
This novel aim to denounce the derogatory terms used to speak about immigrants.
This novel aims at denounce the derogatory terms used to speak about immigrants.
This novel aims to denouncing the derogatory terms used to speak about immigrants.
questions.expl: Aim to + BV, avec le -s de la 3e personne ; the derogatory terms.

questions.q: Choose the correct translation: « Lasse d'être rejetée, Elena a hâte de commencer une nouvelle vie. »
choix: Tired of being cast out, Elena looks forward to starting a new life.
Tired to be cast out, Elena looks forward to start a new life.
Tired of being cast out, Elena looks forward to start a new life.
Tired to being cast out, Elena looks forward to starting a new life.
questions.expl: Tired of + V-ing ; look forward to + V-ing.

questions.q: Choose the correct translation: « Les grands-parents de Sofia prévoient de lui transmettre leurs traditions. »
choix: Sofia's grandparents plan to pass on their traditions to her.
Sofia's grandparents plan passing on their traditions to her.
Sofia's grandparents plans to pass on their traditions to her.
Sofia's grandparents plan to passing on their traditions to her.
questions.expl: Plan to + BV ; to pass on traditions.

questions.q: Choose the correct translation: « Ce photographe a l'intention de mettre en lumière la solitude des familles. »
choix: This photographer intends to shed light on the loneliness of families.
This photographer intends to shed light the loneliness of families.
This photographer intend to shed light on the loneliness of families.
This photographer intends shedding light on the loneliness of families.
questions.expl: Intend to + BV ; to shed light on ; the loneliness.

questions.q: (official timetable) The train ____ at 9:15.
questions.expl: Horaire fixe, officiel : présent simple.

questions.q: (spontaneous decision) "The phone is ringing!" "I ____ it."
questions.expl: Décision prise au moment où l'on parle : will + BV.

questions.q: (visible evidence) Look at the sky: it ____ rain.
questions.expl: Prédiction fondée sur une preuve visible : be going to + BV.

questions.q: (arrangement with a date) We ____ the exhibition on Saturday morning; it is already planned.
questions.expl: Arrangement précis : présent be + V-ing.

questions.q: (promise) Don't worry, I ____ you.
questions.expl: Promesse, offre : will + BV.

questions.q: (already decided last week) We ____ a mural next month.
questions.expl: Intention déjà décidée avant le moment où l'on parle : be going to + BV.

questions.q: (prediction without proof) I'm sure this project ____ the way people see the border.
questions.expl: Prédiction sans preuve concrète : will + BV.

questions.q: (opening time) The exhibition ____ at 10 a.m. next Friday.
questions.expl: Horaire fixe, officiel : présent simple.

questions.q: Which future is used for a prediction based on visible evidence ?
questions.expl: Prédiction fondée sur une preuve visible : be going to.

questions.q: Which future is used for an official timetable ?
questions.expl: Horaire officiel : présent simple.

questions.q: Which future is used for a precise arrangement, often with a date ?
questions.expl: Arrangement précis : présent be + V-ing.

questions.q: Which future is used for a promise or an offer ?
questions.expl: Promesse, offre, décision spontanée : will.

questions.q: Which sentences express a future already decided or arranged ? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: We are going to paint; we decided yesterday.
We are visiting the museum; it is booked.
I'm sure it will rain tomorrow afternoon.
Don't worry, I'll help you with the mural.
Perhaps they will win the match tonight.
questions.expl: Be going to : déjà décidé ; présent be + V-ing : arrangement. Will : opinion, promesse.

questions.q: Which sentences use will correctly, for a promise, an offer or a prediction ? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: Don't worry, I'll help you with that.
I'm sure this project will change things.
Look at those clouds, it will rain (proof).
We will visit the museum on Saturday (booked).
questions.expl: Will : opinion, promesse, offre. Pour un horaire, une preuve ou un arrangement on utilise un autre futur.

questions.q: A student writes: "Look at those clouds, it will rain." What does the teacher correct ?
choix: There is visible evidence: it is going to rain
The verb rain needs an -s after the subject here
Clouds cannot be followed by any verb in future
The future here must be the present simple tense
questions.expl: Preuve visible : be going to + BV.

questions.q: A student writes: "The exhibition will open at 10 a.m. next Friday (official timetable)." What is more accurate ?
choix: The exhibition opens at 10 a.m. next Friday
The exhibition is going to opens at 10 a.m.
The exhibition opening at 10 a.m. next Friday
The exhibition will to open at 10 a.m. Friday
questions.expl: Horaire officiel : présent simple.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct ?
choix: I look forward to the exhibition that opens on Friday.
I look forward to the exhibition that will to open on Friday.
I look forward to open the exhibition on Friday.
I look forward at the exhibition that opens on Friday.
questions.expl: Look forward to + nom ; opens (horaire).

questions.q: (timetable) My cousin's flight from Montreal ____ at 7.40 tomorrow morning.
questions.expl: Horaire de vol : présent simple (évaluation 2).

questions.q: (spontaneous decision) "The phone's ringing!" "Stay where you are, I ____ it."
questions.expl: La copie avait « am going to get » : le professeur corrige en « will get » (décision spontanée).

questions.q: (ingredients already bought) Mia has bought flour, eggs and chocolate: she ____ a cake for her dad's birthday.
questions.expl: Les ingrédients déjà achetés montrent que c'est décidé : be going to.

questions.q: (restaurant booked) I can't come on Friday evening. I ____ dinner with my grandparents; my mum booked the restaurant last week.
questions.expl: La copie avait « have » : le professeur corrige en « 'm having » (arrangement).

questions.q: (prediction, no proof) Experts predict that by 2050 most cars in Europe ____ on electricity.
questions.expl: Prédiction d'experts, sans preuve concrète : will.

questions.q: (visible evidence on the scoreboard) We're losing 4-0 with two minutes left. We ____ this match.
questions.expl: La copie avait « will lose » : le professeur corrige en « are going to lose » (preuve visible).

questions.q: (decided last month) "Have you made up your mind?" "Yes, I ____ to a university in Scotland."
questions.expl: La copie avait « will apply » : le professeur corrige en « 'm going to apply » (décidé le mois dernier).

questions.q: (arranged this morning) Tom ____ the bus tomorrow: his brother is driving him to school.
questions.expl: La copie avait « will not take » : le professeur corrige en « isn't taking » (arrangement).

questions.q: (promise) Promise me you ____ me as soon as you get home.
questions.expl: Promesse : will + BV (après as soon as, présent simple).

questions.q: After "as soon as", the verb takes will: "as soon as you will get home".
questions.expl: Après as soon as, le verbe reste au présent simple : as soon as you get home.

questions.q: The present simple can express a future when the schedule is official.
questions.expl: Futur d'un horaire fixe, officiel, indépendant de la volonté du sujet.
